title: Rotkohl
subtitle: german braised red cabbage with apple and spices
excerpt: Rotkohl is slowly braised German red cabbage with apple, vinegar, and warm spices. It is the essential side dish for roast goose, pork, and game. The colour turns vivid purple and the flavour is sweet-sour and gently spiced. Serves 6.
sourceNotes: A German Christmas and Sunday dinner staple. Red cabbage needs an acid such as vinegar or apple to hold its colour and develop the correct flavour.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freezes very well for up to 3 months. Reheat gently with a splash of water.
recipe.batchNotes: Make a large batch. Rotkohl improves over 2 to 3 days and freezes beautifully.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make 1 to 2 days ahead and reheat. The flavour develops significantly.

glossaryTerms.definition: The natural pigment that gives red cabbage its colour. It turns blue-green in alkaline conditions and stays bright red or purple when acid such as vinegar or apple is added.

content.text: The acid from the apple and vinegar activates the
in the cabbage, keeping it vivid and fixing the colour. Without acid, braised red cabbage turns an unappetising purple-blue. Serves 6.
This is a perfect make-ahead dish. It improves with time and reheats beautifully.
Melt the butter in a large heavy-based saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes until softened.
Add the shredded cabbage, grated apple, vinegar, sugar, bay leaves, allspice berries, caraway if using, and water. Stir well.
Cover and cook over low heat for 60 to 75 minutes. Stir every 15 minutes. The cabbage should be completely tender and reduced in volume by about half.
Remove the bay leaves and allspice berries. Taste and adjust the balance with a little more vinegar for sharpness or sugar for sweetness.
Serve hot alongside roast pork, duck, goose, or any braised meat.

attrs.problem: Cabbage has turned an unpleasant blue-grey colour

content.text: You need more acid. Add another tablespoon of red wine vinegar and stir. The colour will shift back to red-purple within a minute or two.

attrs.problem: Cabbage is still tough after an hour

content.text: Add a splash more water and continue braising. Red cabbage can take up to 90 minutes to become fully tender.
Add vinegar a teaspoon at a time until the sweetness is balanced. The correct taste is sweet-sour in equal measure.

Rotkohl is a fixture on the German Christmas dinner table alongside roast goose or duck. It also appears year-round with pork roasts and game. The dish is sold in jars across Germany, but the home-made version is far better. It takes little effort and transforms almost any roast into a complete meal.
